s0501.literal: In the winter of the tenth month, on guichou day, great rain, hail, and thunder.
s0501.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on guichou day, came heavy rain, hail, and thunder.

s0502.literal: In the eleventh month, on jichou day, an edict said: "We rule the four seas, toiling from sun to sun, thinking to spread the utmost governance, yet the way is not yet reached.
s0502.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jichou day, an edict said: "We rule the four seas and toil from dawn to dusk to bring the realm to the highest order, yet the way is not yet reached.

s0503.literal: Yet chariots and troops go out again and again, military expenses are especially burdensome, and though fodder and grain are pressed forward, levies cannot be collected.
s0503.idiomatic: Armies march out again and again, military costs press hard, and though grain is rushed forward, taxes cannot be collected.

s0504.literal: In midsummer drought harmed the crops; within the capital region it was severe, and the people
s0504.idiomatic: Midsummer drought harmed the crops; within the capital region it was severe, and the people

s0506.literal: [lost] their support, [31] and the year's harvest had no refuge.
s0506.idiomatic: [lost] their support, [31] and the year's harvest had nowhere to rest.

s0507.literal: This is because government and punishments are not ordered, yin and yang are out of measure, and the black-haired people are blocked by hunger—whose feet can the ruler stand on?
s0507.idiomatic: Government and punishments are not in order, yin and yang are awry, and the people are stopped by hunger—on whose feet can the ruler stand?

s0508.literal: Speaking of it stirs thought; the remainder of the blame lies on Our person—grace should be spread to reach the common folk.
s0508.idiomatic: When We think on it, the blame rests on Us—grace should be spread to reach the common folk.

s0509.literal: The ten commanderies Danyang, Wuxing, Jinling, Jianxing, Yixing, Eastern Sea, Xinyi, Chenliu, and Jiangling, [32] and
s0509.idiomatic: The ten commanderies Danyang, Wuxing, Jinling, Jianxing, Yixing, Eastern Sea, Xinnyi, Chenliu, and Jiangling, [32] and

s0511.literal: [the various] offices' grain tax and salary for this year, [33] shall each be remitted by half; the half of the adult levy due shall be reported only at next year's autumn harvest."
s0511.idiomatic: [the various] offices' grain tax and salary for this year [33] shall each be cut by half; the half of the adult levy still due shall be reported only at next year's autumn harvest."

s0512.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, General Who Proclaims Resolution and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou Prince of Hedong, Shuxian, died.
s0512.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, General Who Proclaims Resolution and Southern Xuzhou inspector Prince of Hedong, Shuxian, died.

s0513.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, in the first month, on renwu day, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opener of the Mansion with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Chunyu Liang was made Grand Master of Splendid Merit;
s0513.idiomatic: In spring of the thirteenth year, on renwu of the first month, General of Chariots and Cavalry and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes Chunyu Liang was made Grand Master of Splendid Merit;

s0514.literal: Central Authority General and Protector of the Army Prince of Poyang, Boshan, on his original commission was made Opener of the Mansion with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes;
s0514.idiomatic: Central Authority General and Protector of the Army Prince of Poyang, Boshan, on his existing commission was made opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes;

s0515.literal: General Who Guards the Right and Libationer of the Imperial Academy Prince of Xin'an, Bogu, was made Inspector of Yangzhou;
s0515.idiomatic: General Who Guards the Right and imperial academy libationer Prince of Xin'an, Bogu, was made inspector of Yangzhou;

s0516.literal: Military Adviser General and Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Jin'an, Bogong, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;
s0516.idiomatic: Military Adviser General and Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Jin'an, Bogong, was made Left Vice Director;

s0517.literal: [An] General of the Right and Governor of Danyang Xu Ling was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent;
s0517.idiomatic: [An] General of the Right and Danyang governor Xu Ling was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent;

s0518.literal: [34] Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Xian was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
s0518.idiomatic: [34] Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Xian was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

s0519.literal: On gengyin day, General of Light Chariots and Commandant of the Guards Prince of Yidu, Shuming, was made Inspector of Southern Xuzhou.
s0519.idiomatic: On gengyin day General of Light Chariots and Commandant of the Guards Prince of Yidu, Shuming, was appointed inspector of Southern Xuzhou.

s0520.literal: In the second month, on jiayin day, an edict granted enfeoffment and rank to Zhou's great generals under Sima Xiaonan, including Tian Guang, each in differing measure.
s0520.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin day, an edict enfeoffed Zhou's great generals under Sima Xiaonan, including Tian Guang, each according to merit.

s0521.literal: On yihai day, the imperial carriage personally plowed the sacred field.
s0521.idiomatic: On yihai day the emperor plowed the sacred field in person.

s0522.literal: In the fourth month, on yisi day, the Shixing commandery of Heng Province was divided off as Eastern Heng Province, and Heng Province was made Western Heng Province.
s0522.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on yisi day, Shixing commandery of Heng Province was split off as Eastern Heng Province, and Heng Province was renamed Western Heng Province.

s0523.literal: In the fifth month, on jingchen day, former General Who Pacifies the West Fan Yi was made Central Protector of the Army.
s0523.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jingchen day, former General Who Pacifies the West Fan Yi was made Central Protector of the Army.

s0524.literal: In the sixth month, on xinmao day, the newly appointed Central Protector of the Army Fan Yi was made Protector of the Army.
s0524.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinmao day, the newly appointed Central Protector Fan Yi was made Protector of the Army.

s0525.literal: In the ninth month, on guihai night, a great wind came from the northwest; it tore off roofs and uprooted trees, and great thunder and hail followed.
s0525.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the night of guihai, a great wind rose from the northwest, tore off roofs and uprooted trees, and great thunder and hail followed.

s0526.literal: In the tenth month, on guiwei day, Palace Attendant and Governor of Danyang Mao Xi was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Protector of the Army Fan Yi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing Province.
s0526.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on guiwei day, Palace Attendant and Danyang governor Mao Xi was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Protector of the Army Fan Yi was made General Who Pacifies the West and inspector of Jing Province.

s0527.literal: Poyang Commandery was changed to Wu Province.
s0527.idiomatic: Poyang commandery was renamed Wu Province.

s0528.literal: On renyin day, the state of Dandan sent envoys presenting local products.
s0528.idiomatic: On renyin day Dandan sent envoys with tribute.

s0529.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinsi day, a comet appeared.
s0529.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinsi day, a comet appeared.

s0530.literal: On jihai day, Right Wing General and Commandant of the Guards Shen Ke was made Protector of the Army.
s0530.idiomatic: On jihai day Right Wing General and Commandant of the Guards Shen Ke was made Protector of the Army.

s0531.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year, in the first month, on jiyou day, the High Ancestor was seriously ill.
s0531.idiomatic: In spring of the fourteenth year, on jiyou of the first month, the High Ancestor fell gravely ill.

s0532.literal: On jiayin day, he died in the Hall of Proclaimed Blessings, aged fifty-three.
s0532.idiomatic: On jiayin day he died in the Hall of Proclaimed Blessings, aged fifty-three.

s0533.literal: The testament edict said: "We have been ill since We met this affliction, not yet ten days full; medicine has not cured it, and We have reached the great decline—beginning and end have their fixed portion, what more is there to say?
s0533.idiomatic: The death edict said: "Since this illness began, scarcely ten days have passed; medicine has not cured it, and We have reached the end—life and death have their measure, what more can We say?

s0534.literal: Yet ruling the realm within the four seas for fourteen years, in truth We did not rest though the work was done, and day by day We were cautious—We knew the heavy burden of the altars of soil and grain and recognized the hardship of the royal enterprise.
s0534.idiomatic: Yet We ruled the realm within the four seas for fourteen years and, though the work seemed done, did not rest, growing more careful day by day—We knew the altars' weight and the throne's hardship.

s0535.literal: Yet the borders have many alarms and the living people are not yet governed; We wished to sweep clear the four seas and embrace the eight wilds—Our will had none to follow it, and regret remains in the dark earth.
s0535.idiomatic: Yet the borders are troubled and the people are not yet at peace; We wished to sweep the four seas clean and embrace the eight directions—Our will found no follower, and regret goes with Us to the grave.

s0536.literal: The Crown Prince Shubao, succeeding in the legitimate line, is young in years and flourishing in virtue, inheriting the great foundation—the altars have their lord.
s0536.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shubao, legitimate heir, is young and growing in virtue, and will inherit the great foundation—the state has its lord.

s0537.literal: The lords, ministers, and civil and military within and without—all exhaust heart and strength, together drain arms and thighs, escort the past and serve the present, fulfilling the utmost of loyal devotion, holding office and performing duty, extending and aiding bright achievement.
s0537.idiomatic: Let lords, ministers, and civil and military within and without exhaust their strength, serve the dead and the living with full loyalty, hold office and do their duty, and support the throne with all their power.

s0538.literal: Strive for harmony and do not go against Our intent.
s0538.idiomatic: Keep harmony and do not go against Our wish.

s0539.literal: In all funeral arrangements, affairs follow frugality.
s0539.idiomatic: In all funeral arrangements, let affairs follow frugality.

s0540.literal: Gold and silver ornaments need not enter the coffin; bright vessels for the dead are all to be of tile.
s0540.idiomatic: Gold and silver ornaments need not go into the coffin; grave goods shall all be of pottery.

s0541.literal: Only make thrift fit ritual; do not let extravagance violate measure.
s0541.idiomatic: Be sparing yet keep ritual; do not let extravagance break propriety.

s0542.literal: Replacing the sun with the month already has a general rule; the system for removing public mourning—all follow the old standard.
s0542.idiomatic: The rule of substituting days for months already stands; rules for ending public mourning shall follow the old code.

s0543.literal: The hundred offices in post shall attend once every three days; the provinces and garrisons of the four quarters and the feudatories of five ranks shall each keep their charge and all stop rushing to attend."
s0543.idiomatic: Ministers in post shall attend once every three days; provinces, garrisons, and feudatories of five ranks shall keep their posts and cease rushing to court."

s0544.literal: In the second month, on xinmao day, the posthumous title Emperor Xiao Xuan was presented, temple name High Ancestor.
s0544.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao day, the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoxuan was offered and the temple name High Ancestor was given.

s0545.literal: On guisi day, he was buried at Xianning Mausoleum.
s0545.idiomatic: On guisi day he was buried at Xianning Mausoleum.

s0546.literal: When the High Ancestor was still in the fields, he had great breadth, capacity, and stratagem; when he ascended office, he truly fulfilled Heaven and man's hope.
s0546.idiomatic: While still in private life the High Ancestor showed great breadth, capacity, and stratagem; when he took office he truly fulfilled Heaven and man's hope.

s0547.literal: When the Liang house fell into disorder, the Huainan lands all entered Qi; in the first years of Taikian the High Ancestor's will was to recover the old borders, and he deployed divine strategy, gave the command, and marched out—victories in battle and captures in assault followed in succession, and he regained invaded territory; the achievement was indeed splendid.
s0547.idiomatic: When the Liang house fell into disorder the Huainan lands all passed to Qi; in the first years of Taikian the High Ancestor set his will on recovering the old borders, deployed divine strategy, gave the command, and marched out—victories and captures followed in succession until invaded lands were regained; the achievement was indeed splendid.

s0548.literal: When Zhou destroyed Qi and, riding victory, seized territory, they reached the river's edge again.
s0548.idiomatic: When Zhou destroyed Qi and, riding victory, seized territory, they again reached the river's edge.

s0549.literal: The historian says: The High Ancestor's capacity was broad and thick, and he also had the measure of a ruler of men.
s0549.idiomatic: The historian says: The High Ancestor's bearing was broad and generous, and he had the measure of a true king.

s0550.literal: Emperor Shizu knew the heir was benevolent and weak and could not be passed the precious throne; the High Ancestor stood in the place of the Duke of Zhou, and Emperor Shizu kept in heart the example of Taibo—and when he was displeased, all great affairs were entrusted to him.
s0550.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu knew the heir was mild and weak and could not bear the throne; the High Ancestor stood in the place of the Duke of Zhou, and Emperor Shizu kept Taibo in heart—and when he was displeased, all great affairs were entrusted to him.

s0551.literal: When he succeeded to the enterprise, the myriad affairs were peacefully ordered; he commissioned generals and sent armies, recovered the Huainan lands, and opened and broadened territory, quieting the borders.
s0551.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne the myriad affairs were peacefully ordered; he commissioned generals, recovered the Huainan lands, broadened territory, and quieted the borders.

s0552.literal: He enjoyed the state for more than ten years; will grew great and intent grew lax; at Lüliang the army was overturned
s0552.idiomatic: He ruled for more than ten years; will grew great and intent grew lax; at Lüliang the army was overturned

s0554.literal: [army], [35] and the hosts were greatly lost.
s0554.idiomatic: [army], [35] and the hosts were greatly lost.

s0555.literal: The southeast was weakened—this is the reason.
s0555.idiomatic: The southeast was weakened—and this is why.

s0557.literal: In general his virtue did not reach his letters, his wisdom did not reach his martiality—though gain and loss lay in himself, he had no strategy to meet the enemy.
s0557.idiomatic: In the end his virtue did not match his learning, his wisdom did not match his martial fame—though the outcome lay in himself, he had no strategy to meet the enemy.

s0559.literal: Liang [middle] in the second year of Datong, seventh month, xinyou day, birth—supplemented according to the Basic Annals of Emperor Xuan in the Southern History.
s0559.idiomatic: On "Liang [middle] Datong year 2, month 7, xinyou, birth": supplemented from the Southern History annals of Emperor Xuan.

s0560.literal: Comment: Emperor Xuan died in the first month of the fourteenth year of Taikian, on jiayin day, aged fifty-three; pushing upward from this, it is exactly Liang middle Datong year 2.
s0560.idiomatic: Note: Emperor Xuan died Taikian 14/1/jiayin, aged fifty-three; counting back, that is Liang middle Datong year 2.

s0561.literal: At that time the cavalry commander Li Zong had old ties with the High Ancestor—the Hall edition collation says the Southern History has no character "horse."
s0561.idiomatic: On "cavalry commander Li Zong had old ties with the High Ancestor": the Hall edition notes the Southern History lacks the character horse.

s0563.literal: [firm] swore to the azure heavens—changed according to all editions.
s0563.idiomatic: On "[firm] swore to the azure heavens": emended per all editions.

s0564.literal: Protector of the Army Shen Ke as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guangzhou—comment: Shen Ke only in the sixth month of the second year of Taikian advanced from General of the South and Inspector of Guangzhou to General Who Pacifies the South; this "General Who Pacifies the South" is suspected to read "General of the South."
s0564.idiomatic: On "Protector Shen Ke as General Who Pacifies the South and Guangzhou inspector": Shen Ke was only promoted from General of the South in Taikian 2/6; Pacifies the South here likely should read General of the South.

s0565.literal: Remove its excessive ease—"excessive ease" in all editions reads "ease excessive."
s0565.idiomatic: On "remove its excessive ease": all editions read ease excessive.

s0566.literal: The two tutors, libationers, and below
s0566.idiomatic: The two tutors, libationers, and below

s0568.literal: silk gifts each in differing measure—deleted according to Yuan Gui 260.
s0568.idiomatic: On "silk gifts each in differing measure": deleted per Yuan Gui 260.

s0569.literal: Comment: this is not edict text and should not have the character "may."
s0569.idiomatic: Note: this is not edict text and should not have may.

s0571.literal: Ninth month, gengzi new moon—comment: above already says "eighth month of autumn," so here the character "autumn" should not appear again; now deleted.
s0571.idiomatic: On "ninth month, gengzi new moon": autumn was already given above, so autumn here is deleted.

s0572.literal: Black sable changed to worn—"changed" in Yuan Gui 213 reads "therefore."
s0572.idiomatic: On "black sable changed to worn": Yuan Gui 213 reads therefore for changed.

s0573.literal: End their long stagnation—"their" in all editions reads "body."
s0573.idiomatic: On "end their long stagnation": all editions read body for their.

s0575.literal: Therefore General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Zhaoda received sacrifice in Emperor Shizu's temple court—comment: Zhang Zhaoda in the twelfth month of the third year of Taikian, on renchen day, died in office as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry; above "general" there should be the character "grand."
s0575.idiomatic: On "General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Zhaoda sacrificed in Emperor Shizu's temple": Zhang died in office as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry on Taikian 3/12/renchen; general here should read grand general.

s0576.literal: Ten [one] month, jihai night, earthquake—supplemented according to the Basic Annals of Emperor Xuan in the Southern History.
s0576.idiomatic: On "tenth [eleventh] month, jihai night, earthquake": supplemented from the Southern History annals of Emperor Xuan.

s0577.literal: Comment: above records "winter, tenth month," so here it should not again record "tenth month," and moreover in that year the eleventh month new moon was jihai—clearly one character "one" is missing.
s0577.idiomatic: Note: winter tenth month was already given above, so tenth month should not repeat; that year's eleventh month new moon was jihai—one is clearly missing.

s0578.literal: The Hall edition collation says the Southern History reads "eleventh month" and does not record the new moon; taking the "wuxu" above as proof, there is also suspected corruption.
s0578.idiomatic: The Hall edition notes the Southern History reads eleventh month without new moon; using wuxu above as proof, corruption is suspected there too.

s0579.literal: Now comment: the Southern History is suspected to lack one character "new moon," while the character "night" in this "jihai night" should read "new moon."
s0579.idiomatic: Comment: the Southern History may lack new moon, while night in jihai night should read new moon.

s0582.literal: [hai] Zhou sent envoys to court—comment: above there is yimao, so below there should not be guimao.
s0582.idiomatic: On "[hai] Zhou sent envoys to court": yimao appears above, so guimao below is wrong.

s0583.literal: Zhou sent envoys to court and Huang Faqu's capture of He Province's city on the same day—the Comprehensive Mirror records "guihai, Huang Faqu captured He Province"; thus one knows "guimao" is the error for "guihai"—now changed accordingly.
s0583.idiomatic: Zhou's envoys and Huang Faqu's capture of He Province on one day—the Comprehensive Mirror has guihai for Huang Faqu's capture; guimao is therefore a mistake for guihai—emended.

s0584.literal: Ninth month, jiazi day, Yangping city surrendered—Qian Daxin's Examination of Errors in the Twenty-Two Histories says: "Comment: in the fourth month of that year Yangping Commandery's city surrender was already recorded; here again Yangping city surrenders—there are two Yangpings.
s0584.idiomatic: On "ninth month, jiazi, Yangping city surrendered": Qian Daxin notes Yangping commandery's surrender was already recorded in the fourth month—two Yangpings are meant.

s0585.literal: Examining the Sui Treatise, Jiangdu commandery's Anyi county under Liang set up Yangping Commandery; also the Wei Treatise's Chu Province administered Yangping Commandery, governing Yangping and Puyang counties—or the former is Anyi's Yangping and the latter is Zhongli's Yangping?
s0585.idiomatic: The Sui Treatise has Anyi in Jiangdu under Liang as Yangping commandery; the Wei Treatise has Chu Province's Yangping with Yangping and Puyang counties—perhaps the first is Anyi's Yangping and the second Zhongli's?

s0586.literal: Eastern Wei's Chu Province seat was Zhongli city."
s0586.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Chu Province was seated at Zhongli city."

s0587.literal: Governor of Gaotang Shen Shandu captured Matou city—Qian Daxin's Examination of Errors says "Shen Shandu" in the Comprehensive Mirror reads "Shen Shanqing."
s0587.idiomatic: On "Gaotang governor Shen Shandu captured Matou": Qian Daxin notes the Comprehensive Mirror reads Shen Shanqing.

s0588.literal: General Who Overawes the Barbarians Liu Taogen captured Qushan city—"Liu Taogen" in the Comprehensive Mirror reads "Liu Taozhi."
s0588.idiomatic: On "General Who Overawes the Barbarians Liu Taogen captured Qushan": the Comprehensive Mirror reads Liu Taozhi.

s0589.literal: Hu Sheng's commentary says: "This Liu Taozhi is certainly a Chen general, not Qi's Liu Taozhi."
s0589.idiomatic: Hu Sheng notes: this Liu Taozhi is surely Chen's general, not Northern Qi's Liu Taozhi.

s0590.literal: Comment: this book before and after all writes "Liu Taogen"—the Comprehensive Mirror is suspected to be in error.
s0590.idiomatic: Note: this book consistently reads Liu Taogen—the Comprehensive Mirror is likely wrong.

s0591.literal: The native officials of Liyang and Linjiang commanderies in Southern Yu Province—comment: under "native" in the Jigu edition there is a small note saying one reading is "gentleman."
s0591.idiomatic: On "native officials of Liyang and Linjiang in Southern Yu": the Jigu edition notes one reading is gentleman.

s0593.literal: Chen Taogen again memorialized presenting two hundred pieces each of woven-pattern silk and brocade coverlets—the "again" below "woven-pattern silk" in the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions reads "pattern," and below "brocade coverlets" there is the character "fur" and no "hundred pieces"—
s0593.idiomatic: On "Chen Taogen again presented two hundred pieces each of woven silk and brocade coverlets": the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read pattern for again under woven silk, add fur under brocade coverlets, and omit hundred pieces—

s0594.literal: the Southern Supervisory and Jigu editions have "hundred pieces," the rest the same as the Northern Supervisory.
s0594.idiomatic: the Southern Supervisory and Jigu editions have hundred pieces; the rest match the Northern Supervisory.

s0595.literal: The Basic Annals of Emperor Xuan in the Southern History reads "again" as "pattern."
s0595.idiomatic: The Southern History annals of Emperor Xuan read pattern for again.

s0599.literal: says: "This text is not in error.
s0599.idiomatic: says: "This text is not in error.

s0600.literal: The meaning is that woven-pattern silk and brocade coverlets are two items, two hundred bolts each.
s0600.idiomatic: The meaning is woven silk and brocade coverlets as two items, two hundred bolts each.
